UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

EXHIBIT A — Meta — November 7, 2026 — Final

PLAINTIFF’S INTERROGATORIES TO DEFENDANT META PLATFORMS, INC.

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine, under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1) and 33 and the Court’s Order of [date], ECF No. [__], propounds the following interrogatories on Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”). The date range in each interrogatory is inclusive. Interrogatory No. 1 concerns the complete full legal name, including all three components. Interrogatory No. 2 is an independent account question and has no full-name condition.

Interrogatory No. 1

Did Meta submit to NCMEC, between July 1, 2022 and April 22, 2026, inclusive, any CyberTipline report that, as submitted by Meta, contained or otherwise identified the full legal name “Marvelle J. Ballentine”?

Interrogatory No. 2

Did Meta submit to NCMEC, between July 1, 2022 and April 22, 2026, inclusive, any CyberTipline report in connection with the Facebook account associated with Plaintiff and enforced against on or about July 4, 2022?

Instruction 1. Form and limits of the answer. Answer each interrogatory separately with “Yes,” “No,” or “Unable to determine after reasonable inquiry.” A qualification necessary for accuracy should ordinarily be confined to one sentence; any additional qualification must be concise and limited to what is necessary for a complete, accurate answer. Do not include a report narrative, report number, report date, submitter identity, other report contents, or an explanation of underlying events. These answer limits do not restrict a specific legal objection under Rule 33(b)(4). An inability to determine must follow reasonable inquiry; it is not an alternative to making that inquiry.

Instruction 2. Original report, full name, and account scope. “As submitted by Meta” means the report in the form and content transmitted by Meta to NCMEC, before later supplementation or association. For Interrogatory No. 1 only, “Contained or otherwise identified” means the full name appears in the original report itself, including when the components appear in separate name fields. Ordinary capitalization, spacing, or punctuation differences do not defeat a match. Do not infer that match from another name, an account identifier, or an outside source. In Interrogatory No. 2, “in connection with” means that Meta’s records of the submission associate the report with the specified account, its content or activity, or the enforcement against it. The account is the one Plaintiff operated and against which Meta acted on or about July 4, 2022, whether described as termination, disablement, suspension, or other enforcement. This connection need not appear in a name field or depend on a full-name match. Answer the two interrogatories independently.

Instruction 3. Exclusion of separate and later information. For Interrogatory No. 1, do not use Plaintiff’s April 9, 2026 materials, court filings, public sources, or information obtained or added after original submission to supply a full name absent from that original report. For Interrogatory No. 2, determine the submission’s account connection from Meta’s records of that submission, without treating Plaintiff’s later characterization alone as the connection. Plaintiff’s correspondence does not become a CyberTipline report merely because it appears in a file. This exclusion does not erase a name actually present in an original report merely because the same name also appears in Plaintiff’s materials. No reconstruction of the reporting party’s sources is requested.

Instruction 4. Rule 33 compliance and time. Respond through an officer or agent using information available to the organization under Rule 33(b)(1)(B). Answer under oath as required by Rule 33(b)(3). State any objection with specificity under Rule 33(b)(4), and answer to the extent not objected to. The person answering signs the answers; counsel signs objections under Rule 33(b)(5). Serve the answers and any objections within seven days after service of the authorized interrogatories, or within the period fixed by the Court.
